newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end close to all-time high.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end close to all-time high.

text.p: French stocks closed more than one percent higher on Tuesday and set a new high for the year but fell short of matching their all-time high.
Traders said the bourse was lifted by a stronger dollar and growing expectations of near-term interest rate cuts in Europe.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed 30.48 points or 1.31 percent higher at 2,349.11 -- within reach of its historic record of 2,360.98 set in February 1994.
The CAC-40 futures contract ended the session at 2,352.0, up 30.5 points from its close on Monday.
Volume was a very heavy 8.5 billion francs with 6.3 billion on the blue-chip CAC-40.
"It was hey, ho, it's off to the races we go," said one trader about the busy day.
Dealers said the CAC-40 was likely to rise through its all time high on Wednesday, but said a durable bull run from here depended largely on the U.S. stock market.
Companies with U.S. units, heavy exports toward the United States or in competition with U.S. manufacturers were big gainers during the session thanks to the dollar's surge.
The dollar was worth 1.5662 marks late on Tuesday.
The dollar gained after Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said this week that he had no objection to a higher dollar.
Chief Bundesbank Economist Otmar Issing's prediction on Monday that investors could switch assets into dollars in the early stages of European monetary union also lifted the unit.
New York Federal Reserve Bank President William McDonough echoed Issing's comments early on Tuesday.
"The dollar may take on a bit more relative importance as a reserve currency," in the run up to and in the first years after the start of a single currency, McDonough told a conference.
LVMH shares rose 4.42 percent to 1,394 francs. The flagship luxury goods company was the third-biggest gainer for the day on heavy volume, a chief beneficiary of the dollar's rise.
Other stocks to benefit from the dollar's strength included Elf, up 1.03 percent, Total, up 0.99 percent, Metaleurop, up 3.53 percent and Michelin up 2.87 percent.

Eurotunnel shares were up 2.96 percent to 6.95 francs as the stock rebounded after its tumble due to a fire in the Channel Tunnel two weeks ago. Dealers said short positions in the stock were bought back because of expectations passenger traffic through the tunnel would restart soon.
Credit Lyonnais investment certificates were off 0.95 percent on news of an investigation of the former managers of the troubled state bank.

Shares in Paribas and its unit Cie Bancaire firm 1.72 percent and 4.11 percent, respectively, on rumours that Bancaire, a unit of Paribas would sell a large stake in its Cetelem subsidiary to pay for provisioning Sinvim's real estate exposure.
Cetelem fell 1.27 percent on the rumours.
Bouygues fell 2.76 percent on rumours of a capital increase tied to the purchase of St. Gobain's CISE unit. St Gobain rose 1.6 percent.
